name: Chicken teriyaki
steps: Pat chicken dry. Heat oil over medium heat and cook skin-side down for 6-8 minutes; turn and cook 5-7 minutes until cooked through.
Mix soy, mirin and sugar. Add to the pan and bubble 2-3 minutes, turning chicken until glossy.
Slice and serve over rice with the pan sauce.

name: Salmon shioyaki
steps: Sprinkle salmon with salt and leave 10 minutes; blot dry.
Oil a pan over medium heat. Cook salmon skin-side down 5 minutes, then turn and cook 3-5 minutes until opaque and flaking.
Serve with lemon and rice.

name: Miso soup with tofu
steps: Soak wakame in water for 5 minutes and drain. Cut tofu into cubes and slice the onion.
Bring dashi to a gentle simmer. Add tofu and wakame and heat 2 minutes.
Turn off heat. Dissolve miso in a ladle of broth, stir back in and top with onion.

name: Onigiri with cooked salmon
steps: Flake salmon, removing skin and bones. Let rice cool just until comfortable to handle.
Wet hands and salt them lightly. Divide rice into four portions; place salmon in the centre of each and shape into triangles.
Wrap with nori and eat promptly, or cool quickly and refrigerate.

name: Oyakodon
steps: Thinly slice onion and cut chicken into 2 cm pieces.
Simmer dashi, soy, mirin, sugar and onion for 5 minutes. Add chicken and simmer 8-10 minutes until cooked through.
Pour in beaten eggs, cover and cook 2-3 minutes until set. Spoon onto rice.

name: Gyudon
steps: Slice onion thinly. Bring dashi, soy, mirin and sugar to a simmer.
Cook onion in the broth for 5 minutes. Add beef in loose pieces and simmer 4-6 minutes until cooked.
Divide rice between bowls and top with beef, onions and broth.

name: Vegetable Japanese curry
steps: Cut vegetables into bite-size pieces. Cook onion in oil over medium heat for 5 minutes.
Add carrot, potatoes and water. Simmer 20 minutes until tender.
Turn off heat and dissolve curry roux. Simmer gently 5 minutes, stirring; add water if too thick. Serve with rice.

name: Tonkatsu
ingredients: 2 boneless pork loin steaks (150 g each)
steps: Pound pork to 1 cm thick. Coat with flour, beaten egg and panko in that order.
Heat a 1 cm layer of oil to about 170 C. Fry pork 4-5 minutes per side until golden and cooked through; drain.
Rest 3 minutes, slice and serve with finely shredded cabbage and sauce.

name: Katsudon
steps: Slice onion and cut tonkatsu into strips.
Simmer onion with dashi, soy and mirin for 5-7 minutes. Lay cutlets on top and heat 2 minutes.
Pour beaten eggs around cutlets, cover and cook until set. Serve over rice.

name: Chicken karaage
steps: Cut chicken into 3 cm pieces. Mix with soy, sake, ginger and grated garlic; marinate 15 minutes in the refrigerator.
Drain excess marinade and coat each piece with starch. Heat oil to 170 C in a small deep pan.
Fry in small batches for 5-7 minutes until crisp and cooked through. Drain and serve with lemon.

name: Pan-fried gyoza
steps: Finely chop cabbage and onion. Mix with pork, ginger, soy and sesame oil.
Divide filling between wrappers. Moisten edges, fold and seal firmly.
Heat neutral oil in a lidded pan. Brown gyoza bases for 2 minutes; add water, cover and steam 7-8 minutes until pork is cooked. Uncover and evaporate remaining water.

name: Okonomiyaki
steps: Whisk flour, dashi and eggs. Fold in finely sliced cabbage and chopped cooked shrimp.
Heat half the oil and spoon in half the batter as a thick pancake. Cover and cook over medium-low heat for 5 minutes.
Flip and cook 5-6 minutes until the centre is set. Repeat with remaining batter; finish with sauce and mayonnaise.

name: Yakisoba
steps: Shred cabbage and carrot. Heat oil and stir-fry pork 4-5 minutes until cooked.
Add vegetables and cook 3 minutes. Add noodles and water; loosen with tongs.
Stir in sauce and fry 2-3 minutes until hot throughout.

name: Vegetable yaki udon
steps: Slice mushrooms, cabbage and carrot. Rinse udon briefly to loosen and drain.
Stir-fry vegetables in neutral oil over medium-high heat for 5 minutes.
Add udon, soy and mirin; toss for 3 minutes. Finish with sesame oil.

name: Kake udon
steps: Bring dashi, soy and mirin to a gentle simmer for 3 minutes.
Heat udon according to the pack and drain.
Divide noodles between bowls, pour over broth and add sliced onions.

name: Cold sesame soba
steps: Cook soba according to the pack, rinse under cold water and drain well.
Whisk tahini, soy, vinegar, sugar and water until smooth.
Toss noodles with thin cucumber strips and dressing. Sprinkle with sesame seeds.

name: Easy shoyu ramen
steps: Boil eggs for 9 minutes, cool, peel and halve.
Simmer stock, soy and sesame oil for 5 minutes. Add sliced cooked chicken and heat through.
Cook noodles separately according to the pack and drain. Assemble with broth, chicken, eggs and sliced onion.

name: Kitsune udon
steps: Pour boiling water over aburaage and drain. Simmer in 150 ml of the dashi with half the soy, half the mirin and sugar for 10 minutes.
Heat remaining dashi with remaining soy and mirin. Warm udon according to its pack.
Serve noodles and broth topped with aburaage and sliced onion.

name: Nikujaga
steps: Cut potatoes into 3 cm pieces and slice carrot and onion.
Cook beef and onion in oil for 3 minutes. Add potatoes, carrot, dashi, soy, mirin and sugar.
Simmer partly covered 20-25 minutes until vegetables are tender, turning gently. Rest 5 minutes before serving.

name: Buta no shogayaki
steps: Mix ginger, soy, mirin and sugar. Thinly slice onion and shred cabbage.
Heat oil and cook onion for 3 minutes; add pork and fry 4-6 minutes until cooked.
Add sauce and toss for 2 minutes. Serve with shredded cabbage.

name: Miso-glazed aubergine
steps: Heat oven to 210 C. Halve aubergines lengthways, score flesh and brush with oil.
Roast cut-side up 25 minutes until soft. Mix miso, mirin, sugar and water.
Spread glaze over flesh and roast a further 5 minutes, watching for scorching. Add sesame seeds.

name: Agedashi tofu
steps: Wrap tofu in a clean towel and press gently for 10 minutes. Cut into six pieces and coat lightly with starch.
Heat oil and fry tofu 3-4 minutes per side until lightly crisp.
Simmer dashi, soy and mirin for 3 minutes. Spoon around tofu and add sliced onion.

name: Hiyayakko
steps: Drain tofu carefully and divide between two bowls.
Slice onion very finely and spoon over tofu with ginger.
Drizzle with soy sauce and finish with sesame seeds. Serve chilled.

name: Tamagoyaki
steps: Beat eggs with dashi, sugar and soy. Heat a small nonstick pan over medium-low heat and wipe with oil.
Pour in a thin layer; when nearly set, roll to one side. Oil the empty area, add another thin layer and lift the roll so egg runs underneath.
Roll again; repeat until egg is used. Cook until fully set, rest 2 minutes and slice.

name: Omurice
steps: Dice chicken and onion. Fry in oil for 6-8 minutes until chicken is cooked.
Add rice and ketchup and stir-fry until piping hot. Divide onto plates.
Beat eggs. Melt half the butter in a nonstick pan and make a fully set thin omelette with half the eggs. Lay over rice; repeat for the second serving.

name: Takikomi gohan
steps: Rinse rice, drain and soak in the measured dashi for 20 minutes. Thinly slice mushrooms, carrot and tofu pouch.
Add soy and mirin to rice; place vegetables and tofu on top. Bring to a boil in a lidded pot.
Cover, reduce heat to very low and cook 12 minutes. Turn off heat and rest 10 minutes, then fold together.

name: Ochazuke with salmon
steps: Reheat rice until steaming and divide between bowls.
Flake salmon, remove bones and scatter over rice.
Pour in hot tea, add soy to taste and finish with torn nori and sesame seeds.

name: Cooked salmon chirashi
steps: Dissolve sugar and salt in vinegar, then fold through warm rice. Let cool until just warm.
Flake salmon and slice cucumber and avocado.
Divide rice between bowls, arrange toppings and finish with torn nori. Eat promptly.

name: Cucumber maki
steps: Mix vinegar, sugar and salt and fold through rice. Cool until just warm. Cut cucumber into long thin batons.
Place nori on a bamboo mat and spread half the rice over it, leaving a 2 cm bare edge.
Lay cucumber across the centre, roll firmly and seal edge with water. Repeat and cut each roll into six with a damp knife.

name: Vegetable tempura
steps: Slice sweet potato 5 mm thick, cut pepper into strips and trim beans. Heat oil in a deep pan to 170-175 C.
Stir flours and cold water briefly; some lumps are fine. Dip vegetables in batter.
Fry in small batches for 2-4 minutes until crisp and cooked. Drain and serve with soy sauce diluted with a little water.

name: Chawanmushi
steps: Beat eggs gently with dashi and soy, then strain. Slice mushrooms and divide with chicken between two heatproof cups.
Pour egg mixture into cups and cover each with foil. Place in a pot with hot water halfway up the cups.
Cover pot and steam over very low heat 15-20 minutes until just set with no liquid egg in the centre.

name: Spinach goma-ae
steps: Boil spinach for 45-60 seconds. Cool under cold water, squeeze thoroughly and cut into 4 cm lengths.
Grind sesame seeds and mix with soy and sugar.
Toss spinach with dressing, separating the leaves evenly.

name: Kinpira gobo
steps: Scrub burdock and cut into matchsticks; soak in water 5 minutes and drain. Cut carrot into matchsticks.
Stir-fry both in sesame oil for 5 minutes. Add soy, mirin, sugar and water.
Cook 5-7 minutes until tender with a slight bite and liquid has evaporated. Sprinkle with sesame seeds.

name: Sunomono
steps: Slice cucumber thinly, toss with salt and leave 10 minutes.
Soak wakame in cold water for 5 minutes and drain. Squeeze cucumber gently.
Mix vinegar and sugar, then toss with cucumber and wakame. Serve chilled.

name: Japanese potato salad
steps: Peel and cube potatoes; simmer 12-15 minutes until tender. Add thin carrot slices for the last 3 minutes; drain.
Lightly mash potatoes and mix with vinegar. Slice cucumber thinly, salt and squeeze out excess moisture.
Cool potatoes, then fold in carrot, cucumber and mayonnaise. Chill until serving.

name: Edamame with sea salt
steps: Bring water to a boil and add edamame.
Boil 4-5 minutes or according to the pack, until beans are tender.
Drain and toss pods with salt. Eat only the beans; discard pods.

name: Yakitori chicken skewers
steps: Soak wooden skewers in water 20 minutes. Cut chicken and onion into 3 cm pieces and thread alternately.
Simmer soy, mirin and sugar for 3-4 minutes to thicken slightly.
Brush skewers with oil and grill or pan-fry over medium heat for 12-15 minutes, turning often. Brush with glaze near the end and cook until chicken is cooked through.

name: Tsukune chicken patties
steps: Mix mince, finely chopped onion, ginger, panko and egg. Shape into six small patties.
Heat oil and pan-fry patties 5-6 minutes per side over medium-low heat until cooked through.
Add soy, mirin and sugar; turn patties in bubbling sauce for 2 minutes.

name: Saba misoni
steps: Slice ginger. Mix water, sake, sugar and mirin in a wide pan and bring to a simmer.
Add fish skin-side up and ginger. Cover loosely and simmer gently 10 minutes.
Dissolve miso in some hot liquid and add to pan. Simmer uncovered 5 minutes until fish flakes easily and sauce thickens.

name: Salmon foil parcels
steps: Heat oven to 200 C. Slice mushrooms and onion and divide between two large pieces of foil.
Place salmon on vegetables. Add butter, soy and sake, and seal foil into parcels.
Bake 18-22 minutes until fish is opaque and flakes easily. Open carefully to release steam.

name: Japanese hamburger steak
ingredients: 250 g mixed beef and pork mince
steps: Finely chop onion. Mix mince with onion, panko, milk and egg; shape into two patties.
Brown in oil 3 minutes per side. Add water, cover and cook over medium-low heat 8-10 minutes until cooked through; remove.
Add ketchup and Worcestershire to pan juices. Bubble 1 minute and spoon over patties.

name: Hayashi-style beef rice
steps: Slice onion and mushrooms. Cook in butter for 6 minutes, add beef and cook 3 minutes.
Stir in flour, then gradually add stock, tomatoes, ketchup and Worcestershire.
Simmer 15 minutes, stirring, until sauce thickens and beef is cooked. Serve over rice.

name: Kabocha nimono
steps: Remove seeds and cut squash into 3 cm chunks, leaving skin on.
Arrange skin-side down in a pan. Add dashi, soy, mirin and sugar.
Cover with a loose lid and simmer gently 15-20 minutes until tender. Rest in broth 5 minutes.

name: Kenchinjiru
steps: Drain and crumble tofu. Thinly slice daikon, carrot and mushrooms.
Heat oil and stir-fry vegetables and tofu 4 minutes.
Add dashi and simmer 20 minutes until vegetables are tender. Season with soy and salt to taste.

name: Corn potage
steps: Chop onion and soften in butter for 5 minutes.
Add corn and stock and simmer 10 minutes. Blend until smooth, venting the blender safely for hot liquid.
Return to pan, add milk and salt, and heat gently without boiling.

name: Dorayaki
steps: Whisk eggs, sugar and honey. Fold in flour and baking powder, then water; rest 10 minutes.
Wipe a nonstick pan with oil. Cook small rounds over medium-low heat 2 minutes until bubbles appear, then flip and cook 1 minute.
Cool and sandwich pairs with red bean paste. Makes six small sandwiches.

name: Matcha milk pudding
steps: Sprinkle gelatin over cold water and leave 5 minutes. Whisk matcha with 2 tbsp of the milk until smooth.
Heat remaining milk, cream and sugar until steaming. Remove from heat and stir in matcha and gelatin until dissolved.
Pour into four small cups, cool and refrigerate for at least 4 hours until set.

name: Mitarashi dango
steps: Gradually knead the 85 ml water into flour until soft and pliable; adjust by teaspoons if necessary. Roll into 12 balls.
Boil balls until they float, then 2 more minutes. Transfer to cold water and drain.
Mix remaining ingredients in a small pan and simmer, stirring, until glossy and thick. Coat dango and serve warm.

name: Baked sweet potato
steps: Heat oven to 200 C. Scrub potatoes, dry and prick skins several times.
Bake directly on a tray 45-60 minutes until completely soft; larger potatoes need longer.
Split and serve plain or with butter and flaky salt.

name: Strawberry fruit sandos
steps: Wash and thoroughly dry strawberries. Whip cream and sugar to firm peaks.
Spread cream on two bread slices. Arrange strawberries, add more cream to fill gaps and top with remaining bread.
Wrap tightly and refrigerate 1 hour. Trim crusts and cut with a clean sharp knife.

name: Köttbullar with cream sauce
ingredients: 250 g mixed beef and pork mince
steps: Soak crumbs in milk. Finely chop onion and soften in half the butter. Cool, mix with mince and egg and shape into 16 balls.
Brown meatballs in remaining butter for 8 minutes, turning. Remove, stir flour into pan, then gradually whisk in stock and cream.
Return meatballs and simmer 10 minutes until cooked through. Serve with jam; add boiled potatoes if desired.
alias: köttbullar Swedish meatballs Kottbullar with cream sauce

name: Pannbiff with onions
steps: Soak breadcrumbs in milk. Mix with mince and egg and shape into four patties.
Slice onions and soften in half the butter for 12 minutes; remove. Brown patties in remaining butter 4 minutes per side.
Add stock and soy, return onions and simmer 5-8 minutes until patties are cooked through.

name: Pytt i panna
steps: Dice potatoes, beef and onion into small even cubes.
Fry onion and potatoes in butter over medium heat for 10 minutes until golden. Add beef and cook 5 minutes until piping hot.
Fry eggs separately until set and serve on top with beetroot.

name: Raggmunk
steps: Whisk flour, milk, egg and salt. Peel and grate potatoes and stir into batter.
Fry bacon until crisp and set aside. Heat butter in a pan.
Fry thin potato pancakes 4-5 minutes per side over medium heat until golden and potatoes are cooked. Serve with bacon and jam.

name: Swedish thin pancakes
steps: Whisk flour with half the milk until smooth, then add remaining milk, eggs, salt and half the butter.
Heat a nonstick pan and brush with a little remaining butter. Add a thin layer of batter and swirl.
Cook 1-2 minutes, turn and cook another minute. Repeat; serve with berries and jam.

name: Ärtsoppa yellow pea soup
steps: Rinse peas and soak overnight in the refrigerator; drain. Chop onion and carrot.
Simmer peas, vegetables, water, thyme and marjoram for 60-75 minutes until peas are soft; skim foam and add water as needed.
Season with salt and serve with mustard on the side. This is a meat-free home version.

name: Laxpudding
steps: Heat oven to 190 C. Boil potatoes for 15 minutes until nearly tender, cool slightly and slice.
Butter a small baking dish. Layer potatoes, flaked salmon and dill. Whisk eggs with milk and pour over.
Dot with remaining butter and bake 30-35 minutes until set and lightly golden.

name: Dill-baked salmon
steps: Heat oven to 200 C. Boil potatoes in water 15-20 minutes until tender.
Place salmon in a baking dish, season with salt and top with butter, dill and half the lemon sliced.
Bake 12-18 minutes until fish is opaque and flakes easily. Serve with potatoes and remaining lemon.

name: Creamy dill cod
steps: Slice leek and soften in butter 5 minutes.
Add stock and cream and simmer 3 minutes. Lay cod in sauce, cover and cook gently 7-10 minutes until fish flakes easily.
Stir dill and lemon into sauce. Serve with boiled potatoes if desired.

name: Fiskgratäng
steps: Heat oven to 200 C. Boil potatoes until tender, drain and mash with half the butter and milk.
Melt remaining butter, stir in flour and gradually whisk in stock and cream. Simmer 3 minutes; add dill.
Put fish in a small dish, spoon mash around edges and pour sauce over fish. Bake 20-25 minutes until fish is cooked; add shrimp for final 3 minutes.

name: Toast Skagen
steps: Pat shrimp very dry; chop half. Mix with mayonnaise, creme fraiche, dill and lemon.
Toast bread in butter on both sides.
Spoon shrimp mixture over toast and serve immediately. Keep shrimp chilled until needed.

name: Gubbröra-style egg toast
steps: Boil eggs 9-10 minutes, cool and peel.
Chop eggs and drained ansjovis. Fold with creme fraiche, chives and dill.
Spoon over rye bread. Use the sweet-spiced Swedish sprats, rather than salty Mediterranean anchovies.

name: Janssons frestelse
steps: Heat oven to 200 C. Peel potatoes and cut into thin matchsticks; slice onion.
Butter a small dish and layer potatoes, onion and drained ansjovis, finishing with potatoes. Add cream and 1 tbsp of sprat brine.
Top with crumbs and butter. Bake 50-60 minutes until potatoes are tender; cover if browning too quickly.

name: Sailor's beef stew
steps: Brown beef in butter in a lidded pot; remove. Soften sliced onion for 5 minutes.
Layer sliced potatoes, onions and beef in the pot. Add stock, beer, bay and salt.
Cover and simmer very gently 60 minutes until beef and potatoes are tender. Check liquid occasionally.

name: Kalops beef stew
steps: Cut beef into 3 cm cubes. Brown in butter in a pot, then add chopped onion and cook 4 minutes.
Stir in flour, stock, allspice and bay. Cover and simmer 75 minutes.
Add sliced carrots and simmer 30 minutes until beef is tender, adding water as needed. Remove bay and whole spices before serving.

name: Dillkött-style chicken stew
steps: Cut chicken into 3 cm pieces, slice carrot and leek. Simmer in stock for 20 minutes until chicken and vegetables are cooked.
Whisk flour with water and stir into the broth with cream; simmer 5 minutes.
Add dill, vinegar and sugar. Taste and balance the gentle sweet-sour sauce.

name: Kåldolmar cabbage rolls
steps: Heat oven to 190 C. Blanch cabbage leaves 3 minutes, cool and trim thick ribs. Mix mince, rice, grated onion and egg.
Divide filling between leaves, fold sides inward and roll. Place seam-side down in a buttered dish.
Add stock, brush with syrup and remaining butter, cover and bake 35 minutes. Uncover and bake 15 minutes until filling is cooked.

name: Kålpudding
steps: Heat oven to 200 C. Shred cabbage and fry in butter 10 minutes; stir in syrup.
Mix mince, rice, egg, milk and salt. Spread half the cabbage in a small dish, add mince mixture and top with remaining cabbage.
Bake 35-40 minutes until centre is fully cooked. Rest 5 minutes before serving.

name: Swedish sausage stroganoff
ingredients: 250 g falukorv or mild cooked sausage
steps: Slice sausage into batons and chop onion. Brown both in butter for 6 minutes.
Stir in tomato paste for 1 minute, then add cream, water and mustard.
Simmer 8-10 minutes until hot and slightly thickened. Serve with rice.

name: Oven-baked falukorv
ingredients: 300 g falukorv or mild cooked sausage
steps: Heat oven to 200 C. Slice sausage almost through at 1 cm intervals and put in an oiled baking dish.
Tuck thin apple and onion slices into the cuts. Spread with mustard and scatter over cheese.
Bake 25-30 minutes until hot through and golden. Serve with potatoes if desired.

name: Isterband-inspired sausage plate
steps: Peel and cube potatoes, boil 12-15 minutes and drain. Pan-fry sausages according to the pack until piping hot.
Melt butter in a pan, stir in flour, then whisk in milk gradually. Simmer 4 minutes.
Fold potatoes and parsley into sauce. Serve with sausages and beetroot; use isterband if available.

name: Kroppkakor potato dumplings
steps: Boil peeled potatoes until tender, drain well, mash and cool. Fry chopped bacon and onion; add allspice and cool.
Mix potato, flour and yolk into a soft dough. Divide into eight, flatten, enclose filling and seal.
Lower into gently simmering water. Once floating, simmer 5 minutes more. Drain and serve with melted butter.

name: Hasselback potatoes
steps: Heat oven to 200 C. Place each potato between two chopsticks and make thin cuts, stopping before the base.
Put in a baking dish, brush with half the melted butter and sprinkle with salt.
Bake 40 minutes, brush with remaining butter and add crumbs. Bake 15-20 minutes until crisp and tender.

name: Creamed spinach and eggs
steps: Boil eggs 9-10 minutes, cool and peel. Wilt spinach in a pan, squeeze and chop.
Melt butter, stir in flour and slowly whisk in milk. Simmer 3 minutes.
Fold in spinach, nutmeg and salt; heat 2 minutes. Serve topped with halved eggs.

name: Creamy chanterelle toast
steps: Clean mushrooms and cut large ones. Cook in a dry pan 5 minutes until released water evaporates.
Add butter and cook 4 minutes until golden; stir in cream and salt and simmer 2 minutes.
Toast sourdough and pile mushrooms on top. Finish with parsley.

name: Västerbotten-style cheese pie
steps: Heat oven to 200 C. Rub butter into flour, add water and bring into dough. Press into a 20 cm tart tin and chill 15 minutes.
Prick base and bake 12 minutes. Whisk eggs and cream; fold in grated cheese and pepper.
Pour into shell and bake 25-30 minutes until set and golden. Rest 10 minutes; makes four light portions.

name: Räkmacka shrimp sandwich
steps: Boil eggs 9-10 minutes, cool, peel and slice. Pat shrimp dry.
Spread bread with mayonnaise and cover with washed lettuce.
Arrange eggs, cucumber and shrimp on top. Finish with dill and lemon wedges.

name: Hot-smoked salmon rye toast
steps: Mix cream cheese with dill and lemon.
Spread over rye bread and layer with cucumber ribbons.
Flake salmon, remove any bones and place on top. Serve immediately.

name: Roast beetroot and goat cheese
steps: Heat oven to 200 C. Peel beetroot, cut into small wedges and toss with oil.
Roast 30-40 minutes until tender. Whisk honey and lemon together.
Arrange leaves and warm beetroot, crumble over cheese and walnuts and drizzle with dressing.

name: Swedish cucumber salad
steps: Slice cucumber very thinly and toss with salt. Leave 10 minutes and squeeze gently.
Mix vinegar, water and sugar until dissolved.
Toss with cucumber and parsley. Chill at least 10 minutes before serving.

name: Beetroot apple salad
steps: Dice beetroot and apple into small cubes.
Mix mayonnaise, yogurt, mustard and lemon.
Fold in beetroot and apple. Chill until serving; especially good with meatballs.

name: Mustard dill potato salad
steps: Boil potatoes 15-20 minutes until tender. Drain and halve while warm.
Whisk mustard, vinegar, oil and salt.
Toss warm potatoes with dressing. Fold in dill and sliced onion and serve warm or cool.

name: Nässelsoppa-style spinach soup
steps: Boil eggs for 9-10 minutes, cool and peel. Chop onion and soften in butter 5 minutes.
Stir in flour, then gradually add stock. Add spinach and simmer 5 minutes.
Blend carefully, add cream and heat gently. Serve with halved eggs; spinach replaces nettles in this easy home version.

name: Root vegetable soup
steps: Peel roots and cut into 2 cm cubes. Wash and slice leek.
Soften leek in butter for 4 minutes, add roots and stock and bring to a simmer.
Cook 25-30 minutes until tender. Mash a few pieces to thicken and add parsley.

name: Rotmos root mash
steps: Peel and dice all roots. Simmer swede and carrot in water 10 minutes.
Add potatoes and cook 15-20 minutes until all are very tender; drain well.
Mash with butter and warm milk, then season with salt. Serve as a side for two.

name: Swedish waffles
steps: Heat waffle iron. Whisk flour and baking powder with milk until smooth.
Fold in sparkling water and melted butter.
Cook portions in the iron according to its instructions until crisp and golden. Serve with berries and jam; makes about four waffles.

name: Kanelbullar cinnamon buns
steps: Warm milk until lukewarm. Mix with flour, yeast, 20 g sugar, 30 g butter and cardamom. Knead 8 minutes and prove covered 60 minutes.
Roll to a 25 x 20 cm rectangle. Spread remaining butter, sugar and cinnamon; roll up and cut into eight.
Place on a lined tray, prove 35 minutes, brush with beaten egg and add pearl sugar. Bake at 200 C for 12-15 minutes. Makes eight.

name: Kardemummabullar cardamom buns
steps: Mix flour, lukewarm milk, yeast, 25 g sugar, 30 g butter and 1 tsp cardamom. Knead 8 minutes and prove 60 minutes.
Roll to a rectangle and spread with remaining butter, sugar and cardamom. Fold in half, cut into eight strips and twist each into a knot.
Prove on a lined tray 35 minutes. Brush with egg and bake at 200 C for 12-15 minutes. Makes eight.

name: Kladdkaka chocolate cake
steps: Heat oven to 175 C and line a 20 cm cake tin. Melt butter and let cool briefly.
Stir in sugar and eggs without whipping; fold in flour, cocoa, vanilla and salt.
Bake 18-22 minutes until edges set and centre is slightly soft. Cool completely before slicing. Makes six small slices.

name: Chokladbollar
steps: Mix oats, butter, sugar, cocoa, coffee and vanilla until evenly combined.
Shape into 12 small balls with clean hands.
Roll in coconut and refrigerate 30 minutes until firm. Makes 12.

name: Hallongrottor raspberry cookies
steps: Heat oven to 175 C. Cream butter and sugar, then mix in flour, baking powder and vanilla.
Shape 12 balls and place in small paper cases on a tray. Make a deep thumbprint in each.
Fill indentations with jam and bake 14-17 minutes until pale golden. Cool before eating.

name: Havreflarn oat crisps
steps: Heat oven to 175 C. Melt butter and mix with oats; cool 5 minutes.
Stir in sugar and egg, then flour and baking powder.
Place 12 small well-spaced spoonfuls on lined trays. Bake 7-10 minutes until golden at edges and cool on the tray.

name: Drömmar vanilla cookies
steps: Heat oven to 150 C. Beat butter and sugar, then slowly mix in oil and vanilla.
Fold in flour and baking powder. Shape 16 small balls and set on a lined tray with space between.
Bake 18-22 minutes until set but pale; cool completely. This home version uses baking powder instead of baker's ammonia.

name: Apple crumble with oats
steps: Heat oven to 190 C. Core and slice apples into a small baking dish; toss with cinnamon.
Rub butter into flour, oats and sugar to make a crumbly mixture.
Scatter over apples and bake 25-30 minutes until golden and bubbling. Serve with yogurt; makes four small portions.

name: Blueberry soup
steps: Simmer blueberries, measured water and sugar for 8 minutes.
Stir starch with cold water. Take soup off the heat, stir in slurry, then heat just until the first bubble and remove.
Serve warm or chilled. Adjust thickness with a little water.

name: Rice porridge
steps: Simmer rice with water and salt for 10 minutes until most water is absorbed.
Add milk and cinnamon. Cook over very low heat 30-35 minutes, stirring often to prevent sticking.
Remove cinnamon and serve with sugar. Add milk if you prefer a thinner porridge.

name: Saffron rice pudding
steps: Heat oven to 175 C. Steep saffron in warm milk 5 minutes.
Mix cooled porridge with saffron milk, egg, sugar and almonds. Spoon into a buttered 18 cm baking dish.
Bake 25-30 minutes until set. Serve warm with jam; makes four small portions.

name: Semlor cream buns
steps: Mix flour, lukewarm milk, yeast, sugar, softened butter and cardamom. Knead 8 minutes, prove 60 minutes, then shape eight buns and prove 35 minutes.
Brush with beaten egg and bake at 200 C for 12-15 minutes. Cool, cut off lids and scoop a little crumb from each.
Mash crumb with almond paste and 2 tbsp cream. Fill buns, top with remaining cream whipped, replace lids and dust with icing sugar. Makes eight.

name: Lussekatter saffron buns
steps: Steep saffron in warm milk for 5 minutes and cool to lukewarm. Mix with flour, yeast, sugar and softened butter.
Knead 8 minutes and prove covered 60 minutes. Divide into eight and roll into S-shaped buns; tuck raisins into ends.
Prove 35 minutes, brush with beaten egg and bake at 200 C for 10-13 minutes until golden. Makes eight.

name: Prinsesstårta-inspired berry cups
steps: Cut sponge into small cubes. Whip cream to soft peaks.
Layer sponge, jam, custard and cream in four glasses.
Roll marzipan thinly between baking paper, cut four discs and lay on top. Dust lightly with icing sugar; chill until serving. Makes four, using ready-made components.

name: Miso Swedish meatballs
steps: Soak panko in milk, then mix with mince, egg and half the miso. Shape 16 meatballs.
Brown in butter 8 minutes, turning. Add stock and cream and simmer 10 minutes until cooked through.
Dissolve remaining miso in a little sauce and stir back in with soy. Serve with lingonberry jam.

name: Dill teriyaki salmon
steps: Heat oil over medium heat. Cook salmon skin-side down 5 minutes, then turn and cook 3-5 minutes until flaking.
Mix soy, mirin and honey and add to pan. Bubble 1-2 minutes, spooning sauce over fish.
Remove from heat and finish with dill and lemon.

name: Lingonberry chicken yakitori
steps: Soak wooden skewers 20 minutes. Cut chicken and onions into 3 cm pieces and thread onto skewers.
Simmer jam, soy, water and ginger for 2 minutes.
Brush skewers with oil and pan-fry 12-15 minutes, turning regularly. Brush with glaze in final 3 minutes and cook until chicken is cooked through.

name: Skagen onigiri
steps: Pat shrimp dry and chop finely. Mix with mayonnaise, dill and lemon.
With wet, lightly salted hands, divide warm rice into four portions. Enclose a small spoonful of shrimp filling in each and shape firmly.
Add nori strips. Eat promptly; refrigerate rapidly if not serving immediately.

name: Miso Hasselback potatoes
steps: Heat oven to 200 C. Slice potatoes thinly without cutting through their bases.
Mix melted butter, miso and honey. Brush half over potatoes and bake 40 minutes.
Brush with remaining glaze and bake 15-20 minutes until tender, covering loosely if darkening. Sprinkle with sesame.

name: Katsu rye sandwich
ingredients: 2 small pork loin steaks (120 g each)
steps: Pound pork thin; coat in flour, beaten egg and panko.
Shallow-fry in hot oil over medium heat for 4-5 minutes per side until golden and cooked through. Drain and slice.
Spread bread with mustard, fill with shredded cabbage and pork, and close sandwiches.

name: Dill potato korokke
steps: Boil peeled potato chunks 15-20 minutes, drain well and mash with butter. Cool, then mix with dill and grated cheese.
Form six thick patties; coat in flour, beaten egg and panko.
Shallow-fry in hot oil over medium heat 3-4 minutes per side until golden and hot throughout.

name: Salmon miso dill soup
steps: Simmer diced potatoes and sliced leek in water for 15 minutes until tender.
Add salmon in 3 cm pieces and simmer 5-7 minutes until cooked. Stir in cream and heat gently.
Turn off heat, dissolve miso in a ladle of broth and return. Add dill and serve.

name: Swedish mushroom udon
steps: Slice mushrooms and fry in butter 7-8 minutes until golden.
Add cream, soy and mustard and simmer 3 minutes.
Warm udon according to the pack, drain and toss with sauce. Finish with parsley.

name: Lingonberry gyudon
steps: Simmer sliced onion with stock and soy for 7 minutes.
Add beef, jam and mustard and simmer 4-6 minutes until beef is cooked.
Spoon beef, onions and sauce over hot rice. Add extra jam at the table if desired.

name: Cabbage roll gyoza
steps: Finely chop cabbage and mix with pork, rice, allspice and soy.
Divide between wrappers, moisten edges and seal.
Brown bases in oil 2 minutes. Add water, cover and steam 8 minutes until filling is cooked. Uncover to crisp and serve with jam.

name: Mustard miso chicken
steps: Mix miso, mustard, honey and water.
Pan-fry chicken in oil over medium heat 6-8 minutes per side until cooked through.
Reduce heat, add glaze and bubble gently 2 minutes. Scatter with dill.

name: Beetroot sesame soba
steps: Cook soba according to the pack, rinse cold and drain.
Blend beetroot, tahini, soy, lemon and water into a smooth dressing.
Toss noodles with dressing and finish with dill and sesame seeds.

name: Hot-smoked salmon temaki
steps: Mix vinegar and sugar into warm rice; cool until just warm. Cut each nori sheet in half.
Spread a little rice over one end of each nori piece; add salmon, cucumber strips, cream cheese and dill.
Roll into four cones and eat immediately while nori is crisp.

name: Rye panko cod
steps: Mix both crumbs. Coat fish in flour, beaten egg and crumbs.
Shallow-fry in oil over medium heat 4-5 minutes per side until golden and fish flakes easily.
Mix mustard, yogurt and dill and serve alongside.

name: Soy butter pytt i panna
steps: Dice potatoes, beef and onion. Fry potatoes and onion in butter 10 minutes until golden.
Add beef and soy and stir-fry 4-5 minutes until piping hot.
Fry eggs in a separate pan until set. Serve on the hash with sliced spring onion.

name: Miso cheese gratin
steps: Heat oven to 190 C. Butter a small dish and layer thinly sliced potatoes with minced garlic.
Whisk cream, milk and miso and pour over. Cover tightly with foil and bake 30 minutes.
Uncover, add grated cheese and bake 15-20 minutes until potatoes are tender and top is golden.

name: Ginger dill pork patties
steps: Mix pork, egg, panko, ginger, dill and soy. Form four patties.
Brown in oil 4 minutes per side over medium heat.
Add stock and cream, cover and simmer 8 minutes until patties are cooked through.

name: Kabocha dill soup
steps: Cube squash and chop onion. Soften onion in butter 5 minutes.
Add squash and stock and simmer 20 minutes until tender. Blend carefully and stir in cream.
Remove from heat, dissolve miso in some soup and stir back in. Finish with dill.

name: Swedish curry meatballs
steps: Mix mince, egg and crumbs. Roll into 14 meatballs and brown in oil 6 minutes; remove.
Cook sliced onion in the pan 5 minutes, add water and meatballs and simmer 12 minutes until cooked through.
Turn off heat and dissolve roux. Simmer 5 minutes, stirring. Serve over rice.

name: Miso mushroom barley
steps: Soften chopped onion in half the butter 5 minutes. Add barley and stock and simmer 30-40 minutes until tender, adding water if needed.
Fry sliced mushrooms separately in remaining butter until golden.
Stir mushrooms, miso and cheese into barley off the heat. Finish with parsley.

name: Shrimp dill chawanmushi
steps: Beat eggs gently with dashi and soy; strain. Divide shrimp between two heatproof cups.
Pour in egg mixture, cover cups with foil and place in a pot of hot water halfway up sides.
Cover and steam over very low heat 15-20 minutes until set. Finish with dill and zest.

name: Lingonberry tonkatsu sauce
steps: Pound pork to 1 cm and coat with flour, beaten egg and panko.
Shallow-fry in hot oil 4-5 minutes per side until golden and cooked through, then drain.
Simmer jam, ketchup, soy and water 2 minutes. Slice pork and spoon sauce alongside.

name: Dill cucumber maki
steps: Fold vinegar and sugar into warm rice and cool until just warm.
Spread rice on nori, leaving a 2 cm bare edge. Add cucumber batons, cream cheese and dill.
Roll firmly using a bamboo mat, seal with water and cut with a damp knife. Makes two rolls.

name: Miso aubergine rye toast
steps: Heat oven to 210 C. Dice aubergine, toss with oil and roast 20 minutes.
Mix miso, honey and water, toss with aubergine and roast another 5 minutes.
Toast rye, spread with yogurt and top with aubergine and dill.

name: Potato leek miso soup
steps: Wash and slice leek; peel and cube potatoes. Soften leek in butter 5 minutes.
Add potatoes and stock; simmer 18 minutes until tender. Lightly mash some potatoes and stir in cream.
Turn off heat and stir in miso dissolved in a little broth. Top with chives.

name: Salmon dill okonomiyaki
steps: Whisk flour, water and eggs. Fold in finely shredded cabbage, flaked salmon and dill.
Fry as two pancakes in oil over medium-low heat, covered, 5-6 minutes per side until centres are set.
Mix yogurt and mustard and drizzle over pancakes.

name: Mustard sesame cabbage salad
steps: Shred cabbage finely and cut apple into matchsticks.
Whisk mustard, vinegar, sesame oil and honey.
Toss with cabbage and apple, leave 5 minutes and sprinkle with sesame seeds.

name: Nordic tofu meatballs
steps: Press tofu in a towel 10 minutes, crumble and mix with oats, egg, finely grated onion, soy and allspice.
Rest mixture 10 minutes and form 12 small balls, pressing firmly.
Pan-fry in oil over medium-low heat, turning gently, for 10-12 minutes until golden and set. Serve with jam.

name: Crispy salmon rice cakes
steps: Flake salmon and mix with rice, egg, starch, dill and soy. Shape six firm patties.
Heat oil over medium heat and fry 4-5 minutes per side until golden, set and piping hot.
Finish with lemon juice and serve promptly.

name: Miso butter cabbage
steps: Cut cabbage into four wedges, retaining some core to hold them together.
Brown cut sides in butter over medium heat 3 minutes each. Add water, cover and cook 8 minutes until tender.
Mix miso and honey with a spoonful of pan liquid. Add, turn wedges gently and finish with dill.

name: Japanese Swedish fish bake
steps: Heat oven to 200 C. Arrange sliced potatoes, mushrooms and fish in a small baking dish.
Mix cream, miso and mustard and pour over. Combine panko with melted butter and scatter on top.
Bake 25-30 minutes until fish flakes, mushrooms are tender and topping is golden. Finish with dill.

name: Ginger lingonberry pork
steps: Slice onion and soften in oil over medium heat 5 minutes.
Add pork and ginger and stir-fry 4-6 minutes until pork is cooked.
Add soy, jam and water and bubble 2 minutes until glossy.

name: Dill edamame potato salad
steps: Boil potatoes 15-20 minutes until tender; drain and halve.
Cook edamame according to pack instructions and cool.
Mix yogurt, mayonnaise, mustard, dill and vinegar. Fold through potatoes and edamame and chill until serving.

name: Mushroom miso gyoza
steps: Finely chop mushrooms and cabbage. Fry in butter 8 minutes until moisture evaporates; stir in miso and dill and cool.
Fill wrappers, moisten edges and seal.
Brown bases in oil 2 minutes, add water, cover and steam 6 minutes. Uncover and crisp bases.

name: Matcha cinnamon buns
steps: Mix flour, matcha, lukewarm milk, yeast, 25 g sugar and 30 g softened butter. Knead 8 minutes and prove 60 minutes.
Roll into a rectangle, spread with remaining butter, sugar and cinnamon, roll up and cut into eight.
Prove on a lined tray 35 minutes, brush with egg and bake at 200 C for 12-15 minutes. Makes eight.

name: Black sesame kladdkaka
steps: Heat oven to 175 C and line a 20 cm tin. Melt butter and cool slightly.
Stir in sugar, eggs and sesame paste, then fold in flour, cocoa and salt.
Bake 18-22 minutes until edges are set and centre slightly soft. Cool completely before cutting into six slices.

name: Cardamom dorayaki
steps: Whisk eggs, sugar and honey; fold in flour, baking powder, cardamom and water. Rest 10 minutes.
Cook 12 small pancakes in a lightly oiled pan over medium-low heat, about 2 minutes then 1 minute on reverse.
Soften almond paste with milk and sandwich cooled pancakes in pairs. Makes six.

name: Lingonberry matcha parfait
steps: Whisk matcha with hot water and cool. Whip cream with sugar to soft peaks.
Fold matcha and yogurt into cream.
Layer in four glasses with crushed biscuits and lingonberry jam. Chill until serving. Makes four small portions.

name: Yuzu-style lemon oat cookies
ingredients: 1 tbsp yuzu juice or lemon juice
steps: Heat oven to 175 C. Beat butter and sugar, then stir in zest and juice.
Mix in oats, flour and baking powder. Shape 12 balls and flatten on a lined tray.
Bake 12-15 minutes until golden at edges; cool on tray.

name: Apple miso crumble
steps: Heat oven to 190 C. Slice apples into a small baking dish and toss with cinnamon.
Rub butter and miso into oats, flour and sugar until crumbly.
Scatter over apples and bake 25-30 minutes until golden and bubbling. Makes four small portions.

name: Saffron mochi pancakes
steps: Warm milk with saffron and cool. Whisk flours, baking powder, egg, saffron milk and sugar into a batter.
Heat a lightly oiled nonstick pan over medium-low heat. Spoon six small pancakes.
Cook 3 minutes per side until puffed and fully set; the rice flour gives a pleasantly chewy texture.

name: Black sesame chokladbollar
steps: Mix oats, softened butter, sugar, cocoa, sesame paste and cooled coffee.
Shape into 12 small balls.
Roll in sesame seeds and refrigerate at least 30 minutes until firm.

name: Matcha rice pudding
steps: Simmer rice in measured water 10 minutes. Add milk and sugar and cook over very low heat 30-35 minutes, stirring often.
Whisk matcha with warm water until smooth and stir into pudding off the heat.
Serve with a spoonful of berry jam. Makes two generous bowls.

name: Strawberry cardamom sandos
steps: Wash and dry strawberries. Whip cream, sugar and cardamom to firm peaks.
Spread cream on bread, arrange whole strawberries and fill gaps with cream. Close sandwiches.
Wrap tightly and chill 1 hour. Trim crusts and slice with a clean sharp knife.

name: Miso caramel waffles
steps: Mix flour, baking powder, milk, sparkling water and 40 g melted butter. Cook in a heated waffle iron until crisp.
For sauce, melt sugar with 1 tbsp water in a small pan until amber. Remove from heat and carefully add cream; it will bubble.
Stir in remaining butter and miso, return to low heat until smooth and drizzle over waffles. Makes about four waffles.

name: Dill cheese tamagoyaki
steps: Beat eggs with milk, dill, finely grated cheese and soy.
Heat an oiled nonstick pan over medium-low heat. Pour a thin layer of egg and roll when almost set.
Add further thin layers, lifting the roll to let egg underneath, and roll again. Cook until set and slice.

name: Rye sesame crispbread
steps: Heat oven to 180 C. Mix flours, sesame, salt, oil and water into a firm dough.
Roll very thinly between baking paper, remove top paper and score into 12 pieces. Prick with a fork.
Bake 20-25 minutes until dry and crisp, rotating tray halfway. Cool completely before storing.

name: Blueberry amazake cups
steps: Soak gelatin in cold water 5 minutes. Simmer blueberries with sugar 4 minutes, then divide between four cups.
Heat milk and amazake until steaming; remove from heat and dissolve gelatin in it.
Pour over blueberries, cool and refrigerate 4 hours until set. Use non-alcoholic rice-koji amazake; makes four.

name: Almond anko semla cups
steps: Cut cake into cubes and divide between four glasses.
Mash almond paste with 2 tbsp cream. Whip remaining cream with cardamom and icing sugar.
Layer almond mixture, anko and whipped cream over cake. Chill until serving. Makes four small cups.
